question.text: How many New World screwworm cases will be confirmed in Mexico in total before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the total number of animal cases of New World screwworm in Mexico before July 1, 2027, according to the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) [Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service current status report](https://www.aphis.usda.gov/livestock-poultry-disease/stop-screwworm/current-status?page=1), rounded to the nearest 500.
question.fine_print:
The map and list of cases is updated on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 5:00 p.m. ET by the USDA. This question will resolve as the total number of animal cases on the latest report before July 1, 2027, provided this is published at the earliest by June 1, 2027.

If the USDA ceases reporting or significantly changes its criteria such that previous reporting is not comparable, this question will be **annulled**.

research:
## Research summary: confirmed New World screwworm cases in Mexico (as of 2026-11-05)

**The short version:** Mexico had about **50,667** cumulative animal cases as of Oct 31, 2026. That is already above the question's 30,000 floor. Cases were being added at roughly **1,100 a week** through late October. Last winter the weekly rate fell to about a third of that.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-04: I fetched the USDA APHIS current-status page. It was last modified Nov 4, but the Mexico map and case list showed only "Loading...", so I could not read the count. The page says the map updates Tuesdays and Thursdays at 5 p.m. ET. Mexico's figures come from SENASICA, Mexico's animal health agency, and the page's link to SENASICA returns a 404. Under SENASICA's definition, a case is active at diagnosis and becomes inactive 15 days later if no new wounds or larvae are found. [APHIS](https://www.aphis.usda.gov/livestock-poultry-disease/stop-screwworm/current-status?page=1)
- The USDA's past figures (20,591 on Apr 15, 26,216 on Jun 4) fit the SENASICA cumulative series counted from Nov 20, 2024. This suggests USDA mirrors SENASICA, but I have not confirmed it directly.

### 2. Current status
- 2026-10-31: SENASICA reported **50,667 cumulative cases** since Nov 2024 (28,626 of them cattle) and **1,958 active**. Active cases by species: cattle 1,019, dogs 567, horses 129, pigs 92, goats 70, sheep 66, cats 13, wildlife 2. [Zolo Noticias](https://www.zolonoticias.com/2026/11/02/chihuahua-reporta-130-casos-activos-de-gusano-barrenador-al-cierre-de-octubre/)
- 2026-11-03: Active cases fell to 1,966 from 2,037 on Oct 28. No cumulative figure was given. [Correo](https://periodicocorreo.com.mx/vida-publica/2026/nov/03/guanajuato-inicia-el-mes-con-repunte-de-casi-90-casos-activos-de-gusano-barrenador-170673.html)
- Nothing settles the question yet. The total keeps rising, and only the level reached by late June 2027 matters.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Arizona confirmed its second case, a horse near Hereford in Cochise County. Sonora has more than 70 active cases. [KJZZ](https://www.kjzz.org/fronteras-desk/2026-11-03/arizona-reports-2nd-new-world-screwworm-case-in-cochise-county)
- 2026-11-03: New Mexico confirmed five more cases, and its infested zone now runs from the Bootheel to Doña Ana County. [KRQE](https://www.krqe.com/news/new-mexico/new-mexico-agriculture-officials-update-new-world-screwworm-surveillance-map/)
- 2026-11-02: Chihuahua and Oaxaca are tied for the most active cases (130 each). Chiapas has the most cumulative cases (8,185). [Zolo](https://www.zolonoticias.com/2026/11/02/chihuahua-reporta-130-casos-activos-de-gusano-barrenador-al-cierre-de-octubre/)
- 2026-11-02: The US has 71 cases (18 active), including the first Arizona case (a dog, Oct 28). USDA is reopening border ports to Mexican cattle in phases (Douglas Aug 24, Santa Teresa Sep 24, Columbus Oct 26) and plans Nogales for Nov 30, then about one port a month. [DTN](https://www.dtnpf.com/agriculture/web/ag/livestock/article/2026/11/02/new-world-screwworm-found-arizona)
- 2026-10-23: Mexico has had 663 human cases and 8 deaths in 2026. These are human cases and are not part of the animal count. [El Universal](https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/nacion/registran-663-casos-de-infeccion-por-gusano-barrenador-en-lo-que-va-de-2026-hay-ocho-muertos/)
- 2026-06-27: The Metapa sterile-fly plant in Mexico opened and is ramping up toward 100 million flies a week. [Meat+Poultry](https://www.meatpoultry.com/articles/33716-usda-opens-sterile-fly-facility-in-mexico-to-combat-new-world-screwworm)

Sources: [Jan 2 and Feb 18 (search summary)](https://www.excelsior.com.mx/nacional/aumentan-68-casos-activos-barrenador-enero), [Informador, Jan 20](https://www.informador.mx/mexico/mexico-suma-mas-de-14-mil-casos-de-gusano-barrenador-del-ganado-20260122-0154.html), [CBS, Jun 4](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/flesh-eating-screwworm-detected-25-miles-us-border-usda/), [UnoTV, Aug 18](https://www.unotv.com/salud/gusano-barrenador-alcanza-30-estados-en-mexico-que-estados-no-registran-casos/), [Publimetro, Aug 23](https://www.publimetro.com.mx/noticias/2026/08/25/cuantos-casos-de-gusano-barrenador-hay-en-sonora-ya-suman-cinco-en-el-estado/), [Segundo a Segundo, Oct 24](https://segundoasegundo.com/chihuahua-reporta-133-casos-activos-de-gusano-barrenador-del-ganado/)

- **Seasonality:** Last winter (Dec to Feb) weekly additions dropped to about 350-450, roughly a third of the summer and autumn rate. Active cases fell 57% between Dec 10, 2025 and Jan 7, 2026. [Zeta](https://zetatijuana.com/2026/01/caen-57-casos-de-gusano-barrenador-en-mexico-afirma-sader/)
- **Higher starting point this year:** Active cases are now about 1,960, compared with about 692 on Jan 2, 2026 and 941 on Nov 21, 2025. [La Razón](https://www.razon.com.mx/mexico/2025/11/21/senasica-informa-que-mexico-vigila-941-casos-de-gusano-barrenador-y-contiene-la-plaga-en-el-sur-sureste-del-pais/)
- **Arithmetic only, not a forecast:** about 34.5 weeks run from Oct 31 to late June 2027. At a steady rate, the total would reach:

| Weekly rate | Total by late June 2027 |
|---|---|
| 400 | about 64,500 |
| 700 | about 75,000 |
| 1,130 | about 90,000 |

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market or expert forecast on Mexico's cumulative animal cases.
- Related markets:
  - Polymarket, "Screwworm National Emergency declared by Dec 31": 13.5% Yes.
  - Kalshi, US human screwworm cases in 2026 above 0: 19%.
- The other markets you listed (New Mexico election, tariffs, GDP and so on) have nothing to do with this question.

### 6. Upcoming events
- Winter 2026-27 is the main factor: case growth likely slows from December to February and picks up again around April to June, as it did in 2026.
- Metapa sterile-fly output should keep rising toward 100 million a week. The Edinburg production plant is not due until about November 2027, after this question resolves. [APHIS](https://www.aphis.usda.gov/animals/animal-health/livestock-and-poultry-disease/stop-screwworm/sterile-fly-production-dispersal)
- Planned port reopenings (Nogales Nov 30, then about monthly) could be paused if cases rise.
- **Reporting risk:** the SENASICA link on the APHIS page is broken. If USDA stops posting Mexico counts or changes how it reports them, the question would be annulled.

The page links to SENASICA's Power BI dashboard for Mexico data. The map updates Tuesdays and Thursdays at 5 p.m. ET. [APHIS](https://www.aphis.usda.gov/livestock-poultry-disease/stop-screwworm/current-status?page=1)

## 2. Current status

- 2026-10-31: The total was 50,667, with 1,958 active (1,019 cattle, 567 dogs, 129 horses). [Segundo a Segundo](https://segundoasegundo.com/chihuahua-reporta-130-casos-activos-de-gusano-barrenador-al-cierre-de-octubre/); [Tierra Fuerte](https://tierrafuerte.mx/archivos/87272)
- The total is already above the question's 30,000 lower bound. To reach about 75,000 by July 1, 2027 would take roughly 24,000 more cases in about 240 days, which is about 100 per day.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Arizona confirmed its second case, a horse near Hereford in Cochise County. Sonora is reported to have more than 70 active cases. [KJZZ](https://www.kjzz.org/fronteras-desk/2026-11-03/arizona-reports-2nd-new-world-screwworm-case-in-cochise-county)
- 2026-11-03: New Mexico reported five new cases, and its infested zone now runs from the Bootheel to Doña Ana County. [KRQE](https://www.krqe.com/news/new-mexico/new-mexico-agriculture-officials-update-new-world-screwworm-surveillance-map/)

- 2026-10-22: Mexico reported 663 human cases and 8 deaths in 2026 (through Oct 16). These are human cases and do not count toward this question. [Informador](https://www.informador.mx/mexico/registran-663-casos-de-infeccion-por-gusano-barrenador-en-humanos-en-el-2026-20261022-0196.html)

- 2025-09-27: about 7,437 total. [Por Esto](https://www.poresto.com/campeche/2025/10/3/campeche-registra-mas-de-500-casos-de-gusano-barrenador-en-el-ganado.html)

- 2026-11-02: 50,820 total, about 170 per day.
- Trend: the rate has never fallen. It was slower in the cooler months (roughly 60 to 85 per day from late 2025 to spring 2026) and peaked at 145 to 170 per day from summer to autumn 2026. Active cases are flat at about 1,900 to 2,000, compared with 757 in Nov 2025 (date uncertain) and 1,295 in April 2026.
- Simple projections from 50,820, over about 240 days to late June 2027 (my arithmetic, not a forecast):
  - 80 per day gives about 70,000
  - 120 per day gives about 80,000
  - 170 per day gives about 91,500

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket "Screwworm National Emergency declared by Dec 31": 13.5% Yes. This is related but is not the same question.
- Kalshi, US human screwworm cases in 2026: "Above 0" is 19%. Also not a match.
- I found no market or expert forecast on Mexico's cumulative animal case count.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The winter of 2026-27 may slow transmission, as it did last winter. The spread into northern states such as Chihuahua and Sonora may behave differently in cold weather.
- Sterile fly supply is described as limited. Rumors put USDA dispersal at 100 million per week, and new production capacity (for example the planned Texas and Metapa facilities) could change suppression. [RFD-TV](https://www.rfdtv.com/usda-expands-new-world-screwworm-surveillance-as-cases-rise-in-mexico-and-sterile-fly-supply-stays-limited?p=112)
- Spring and summer 2027 will probably bring higher rates again, if 2026 is a guide.
- Risks to how the question resolves: changes to USDA reporting, which would annul it, and possible gaps between the USDA widget and SENASICA figures.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** about 7.8 months. The last eligible USDA report comes out in late June 2027, roughly 34 to 35 weeks from the latest data point.

(b) **Latest known value:** 50,667 cumulative animal cases in Mexico on Oct 31, 2026, per SENASICA. USDA appears to mirror this series. There were about 1,960 active cases at that point.

(c) **If nothing changed:** about 50,500. This is not realistic, because the cumulative count can only rise.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** at about 1,130 new cases a week, the total would reach about 90,000. A seasonally adjusted path looks like this:
- the rate falls to about 550 a week in January and February;
- it recovers to 1,100 to 1,300 a week by May and June;
- that adds about 29,000 to 30,000 cases, for a total near 80,000.

(e) **Historical variation:** weekly additions have ranged from about 350 a week (winter 2025-26) to 1,180 a week (summer 2026), a factor of about 3. Last year, from about November to June, the total roughly tripled while the area affected expanded. This year Mexico is largely already infested, and sterile fly output from Metapa is rising. Both factors probably dampen growth relative to last year's pattern, but the starting active-case base is about twice as high.

(f) **Experts and markets:** there are no direct forecasts or markets on this quantity. The question creator's range is 30,000 to 100,000.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- *Low:* a sharp winter drop plus effective sterile fly saturation keeps additions around 300 to 400 a week all season. The total would be about 62,000 to 65,000.
- *High:* the northern spread intensifies and spring brings a higher peak than 2026, around 1,800 to 2,000 a week by May and June. The total would be 105,000 to 120,000 or more.

Spread into the colder northern states such as Chihuahua and Sonora suggests a winter slowdown there, while Chiapas and Oaxaca keep producing cases all year.

(f) There are no expert or market forecasts on this quantity. Related markets, such as Polymarket's US national emergency market at about 13.5%, point to continued concern but do not translate directly into a case count.

(g) Low scenario: a harsh winter combined with a fully ramped Metapa plant (100 million sterile flies a week) and stronger control could push weekly additions to about 250 to 400 and keep them there through spring. That would leave the total near 60,000 to 65,000.
High scenario: a mild winter and continued northward spread could keep weekly additions above 1,300, with a spring surge. That would bring the total to 100,000 or more.
